question: Should OpenClaw adopt this two-layer deny-over-allow exec policy, including fail-closed analysis and changed `security=full`/`ask=off` behavior?
rationale: Even after the concrete cross-runtime defects are repaired, the permanent authorization semantics, persisted configuration ownership, and upgrade expectations require explicit maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt a complete narrow contract
options.body: Approve the policy after every TypeScript and native macOS approval owner preserves and enforces it while implementation helpers remain internal.

options.title: Accept a broader public contract
options.body: Intentionally own the helper exports, both persisted configuration surfaces, and changed full/off behavior as long-term compatibility commitments.

options.title: Pause the feature direction
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open and do not land another permanent exec policy surface yet.

recommendation.title: Adopt a complete narrow contract
recommendation.body: Approve the policy after every TypeScript and native macOS approval owner preserves and enforces it while implementation helpers remain internal.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history shows direct ownership of the current native exec approval architecture, policy persistence, and node defaults involved in this decision.
